newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end down sharply on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end down sharply on liquidation.

text.p: Active long fund liquidation and other technical and fundamental pressure knocked CME live cattle futures to sharply lower closes despite limit gains in neighboring pork complex pits. Feeder cattle followed with higher corn futures adding to weakness, traders said.
Live cattle closed 1.225 to 0.375 cent per lb lower with April off 1.225 at 67.475 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.250 to 1.100 cent lower with May off 0.900 at 68.450 cents.
Commercial selling sparked the downturn in live cattle after a higher start, with liquidation prompted by large open interest in April touching off sell stops, traders said.

"We have liquidation of the April contract - you are starting to see some of that as we get closer to the first of April and people try to get their positions in line ahead of the first notice day," said Paul Georgy, president of Allendale Inc.
Georgy noted that liquidation was evident despite firmer cash markets. "Cash markets are strong," he said.
Traders anticipate a continuation of the break Friday following weakness in cash cattle markets early Thursday and the need to further liquidate positions in April.
"It's going to take a long time to get this (April) open interest down," said Art Paulsrud, analyst for ADM Investor Services.

Packers were backing away from fed cattle bids late Thursday after paying $68 per cwt earlier in the day and some cattle sales at $67 Thursday turned fundamental sentiment negative. This, along with the fund liquidation, turned technicals down with sell stops touched off along the way, they said.
Action in pork complex futures, following the news of a foot and mouth disease outbreak in Taiwan hogs, provided only initial spillover support, they said.
Feeders followed live cattle with the rally in corn futures also weighing on the market. Feeders had started up on buy stops but fell sharply as sell stops added to later weakness, they said.
"Corn prices are sharply higher so that is another thing that is impacting the cattle market as well," Georgy added.
Refco, RBH and R.J. O'Brien notably sold live cattle on the early break with Cargill Investor Services a seller late. In live cattle options, R.J. O'Brien bought June 62 puts early.
Commission houses were on both sides of April 68 calls and puts, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.05 at $68.45 per cwt.
